claims.statement: For uniform s in [1,r), input T=[s]P0 and powers A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..n with n dividing r-1, the Cheon auxiliary-input algorithm in proof.md recovers s with probability 1 (deterministic; no randomness, no heuristic assumption) using total work W(n) target-group-operation equivalents as defined in proof.md, Section 6, including preprocessing, advice construction (none), all trials and failures, randomness (none), arithmetic, sorting and lookup, memory transfers, verification and output. At the scoring value n=2^20, W(2^20) has log2 at most 122.759104. Peak memory is at most 2^125.128985 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^122.402707 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps or heuristic assumptions. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic argument, not a claim of practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check the two-phase Cheon BSGS logic and the b-adic table evaluation on small additive cyclic groups of prime order q with d | q-1. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon auxiliary-input attack with BSGS and b-adic scalar tables
